clue.text: Change behind counter emptied out, money in the bank

indicators.note: behind places the word for change after the other piece, so it is read second
a word emptied out has lost its insides, so only its first and last letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of counter
to edit something is to change it

explanation.surface: A cashier swaps notes behind an empty counter while savings sit safely in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is a positive balance held in an account, funds a customer has available to draw on.

clue.text: Background, where tracks heard?

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how the phrase is spoken rather than how it is written

parts.note: routes are the ways tracks run, said the British way to rhyme with boots

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a person's background and where the paths they took can be traced.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English ROUTES is pronounced exactly like ROOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Your roots are your origins, family and upbringing, the history that forms your personal background.

clue.text: Help out when bend is too tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the words beside it come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A driver needs a helping hand because a corner on the road is too difficult to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's bit is an idiom for making one's own contribution to a shared effort.

clue.text: Pack first of oranges inside pastry case

indicators.note: inside puts that letter within the walls of the next piece

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with a filling

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of oranges

explanation.surface: A baker slips a slice of orange into a pastry shell before baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Pack here is a pack of cards, not a verb about packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a deck of special cards used for fortune telling, so it is a kind of card pack.

clue.text: Fairly generous plate of food from women's group?

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British community organisation for women
a dish is a plate of food

explanation.surface: A women's club serves up a reasonably generous helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is placed first and the wordplay reads in reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Widish means somewhat wide, and wide margins or allowances are generous ones.

clue.text: Electrical work interrupted by the scornful

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so another word goes in its middle

parts.note: wiring is the job of an electrician
taken as written

explanation.surface: An electrician's job keeps getting disrupted by sneering onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: The scornful looks like a noun, a group of people, but the definition is the adjective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A withering look or remark is contemptuous, intended to make someone feel small.

clue.text: Flag duly rising on our pole, first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word in the phrase

parts.note: the initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A flag is duly hoisted up the pole before anything else happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is a verb meaning to tire or sag, not the banner the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to lose energy and sag, which is exactly what drooping means.

clue.text: Propose a funny article for programme

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone pitches a humorous piece to fill a slot in a broadcast schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama shown on television or radio as a regular show.

clue.text: Jump well

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a natural source of water rising from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Well looks like an adverb praising the jump, but it is a noun, a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is a verb for leaping upward and a noun for water emerging naturally from underground.

clue.text: Great big toe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a great, a famous figure in some field
second meaning, read cryptically: the big toe is at the end of the leg

explanation.walkthrough: Great and big look like a pair of adjectives describing a toe; the question mark warns that the second meaning is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a celebrated figure, a great of sport or music, and LEG END humorously describes a toe's position.

clue.text: Picture stolen in Picasso, only frame remaining?

indicators.note: in places the word for stolen within the other piece
with only the frame left, the painter's name keeps just its outside letters

parts.note: the outer letters of Picasso
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Thieves have cut a Picasso out of its frame, leaving only the empty frame on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, an image captured by a camera, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: A relation's skewed thinking

indicators.note: skewed means twisted out of true, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A family member has a distorted way of seeing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind a decision, the thinking that justifies it.

clue.text: Check fly, say, with pants originally buttoned up

indicators.note: buttoned up means fastened inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a fly is an example of an insect

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of pants

explanation.surface: Someone checks their trouser fly is done up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The fly, trouser fastening in the surface, is the insect in the wordplay; pants are underpants in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine something closely for faults, which is to check it.

clue.text: Investigate kiss stolen by crafty eloper

indicators.note: something stolen by another is taken into it, so it sits inside
crafty suggests cunning reworking, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
X is the written symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A sly runaway lover snatches a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore is to travel through or examine something in order to learn about it.

clue.text: Biscuit, a blue one behind green, initially

indicators.note: behind puts the earlier pieces after the green letter in the answer
initially asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of green
taken as written
blue jokes are ribald ones, rude and risqué
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone describes the colours of a biscuit, blue and green.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue means smutty here, not a colour. A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with a layer of currants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garibaldi is a flat British currant biscuit named after the Italian general.

clue.text: Journalist entering fray, cut

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy disturbance or row
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter dives into a brawl and gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut is a noun here, as in a pay cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a decrease in size or amount, the same as a cut in prices or staff.

clue.text: Get fifty in team for easy victory

parts.note: to land a job is to get it

indicators.note: in places the number letter within the word for team

parts.note: a side is a sports team
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A batter scores fifty runs and the team wins comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming win, especially in an election, by a huge margin.

clue.text: Fear gone, leader of revolution embraced

indicators.note: embraced means held within arms, so one piece is hugged by the other

parts.note: dead means gone, passed away

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of revolution

explanation.surface: Fear has evaporated now that the rebel chief has been welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a strong sense of apprehension about something to come, which is fear.

clue.text: Result of impact around adjustment of remit, disadvantage

indicators.note: around puts the first piece outside the reordered letters

parts.note: a dent is what an impact leaves behind

indicators.note: an adjustment changes the arrangement, so the word that follows is reordered

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An official reports the effect of changing a body's remit as a drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or damage, a state of being worse off, so it is a disadvantage.

clue.text: I'd put in stake behind washer!

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: a stake is a bet
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone who has placed a bet tucks the betting slip behind a washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind is the noun, the backside, so a behind washer is a cleaner for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin used for washing one's bottom, humorously called a washer of behinds.

clue.text: Castigate scoundrel punching worker, for example

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a worker is one example of a bee
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A rogue hits an employee and gets a severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker refers to the worker bee, not an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to scold them angrily, and castigating is severe reprimand.

clue.text: Dark horse, frightful prospect

parts.note: the dark is the night
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: An unknown competitor in a race could be a scary prospect for the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: Dark horse looks like the idiom for an unexpected contender, but the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a terrifying experience or situation, something dreadful to face.

clue.text: What gets left in bottom of bottle, say

indicators.note: the bottom of a word, in a down entry, is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of bottle
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone describes the dregs left at the bottom of a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Left means bequeathed in a will, not remaining as dregs.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is everything a person owns at death, the property they leave to heirs.

clue.text: More than one of those followed when crepe is cooked?

definitions.text: More than one of those followed when crepe is cooked?

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or falsified, so the words beside it are reworked

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cook follows several sets of instructions when making a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while the last words also supply the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are the instructions a cook follows, so plural ones are what someone making crepes uses.

clue.text: In which one might have a straight index finger, perhaps?

definitions.text: In which one might have a straight
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game in which a straight is a winning hand
second meaning, read playfully: something you prod people with

explanation.walkthrough: A straight is a run of five consecutive cards; the second meaning is a whimsical reading of a thing that pokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is the card game featuring straights and flushes, and an index finger is a tool for jabbing.

clue.text: Canine hurt, darling

parts.note: to whip someone is to hurt them
pet is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Someone comforts a beloved dog that has been injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slender racing breed of dog, so it is a canine.

clue.text: Footballer's partner riding horse-drawn vehicle

parts.note: a WAG is one of the wives and girlfriends of British footballers
riding on a horse is being on it

explanation.surface: A footballer's girlfriend takes a ride in a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled cart pulled by horses for carrying loads.

clue.text: Flier unremarkable, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this asks us to go by what we hear, not by how it is written

parts.note: plain means ordinary and unremarkable

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pilot or aircraft as rather ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is an aircraft, something that flies through the sky.

clue.text: Moment where learner cuts identical card

parts.note: twins are identical

indicators.note: cuts means slicing into, so the learner letter goes inside the card

parts.note: a king is a playing card
L for learner, from British L-plates on learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: A learner driver cuts up an identical card at a decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In the twinkling of an eye means in an instant, so a twinkling is a very brief moment.

clue.text: Effect in fact can echo back

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read from right to left
in tells us the letters are sitting within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning fact, can and the start of echo

explanation.surface: A claim that a fact can be repeated back with impact.
explanation.walkthrough: Effect is a verb here, meaning to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a law or plan is to bring it into effect, so it means to effect.

clue.text: Ten confused about English course

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the number's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
re means about or concerning
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Ten people are unsure about an English class.
explanation.walkthrough: Course means part of a meal, not a programme of study.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served as part of a meal, the main course in some usage.

clue.text: Bottom three frantic by end of season

indicators.note: frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

indicators.note: end of asks for only the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of season

explanation.surface: A team sits in the bottom three, desperate as the season ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or underneath, as in nether regions, so it is an adjective for bottom.
